evals.prompt:
Scope a GitHub webhook -> Slack PR summaries service for MechaSwift. I've pre-answered every clarifying question below so you have no need to ask anything — proceed straight through the full scope flow in this single turn: propose 2-3 approaches with trade-offs, recommend one, briefly present the design, WRITE THE SPEC FILE to references/specs/2026-04-07-github-webhook-slack-summaries.md (I am pre-approving the design so you can write on this turn), do the self-review, ask me to review the spec, then offer what's-next options. Be concise — short sections are fine.

Purpose: surface PR activity in Slack so reviews don't stall. Internal eng team (~15 people).

Pre-answered decisions (do not re-ask):
- Runtime: Node.js + TypeScript, long-running service on our existing Fly.io (NOT serverless). Redis available on Fly.
- Slack bot token already provisioned with chat:write.
- GitHub webhook with HMAC signature verification via shared secret.
- Events forwarded: opened, ready_for_review, closed (per-repo configurable).
- Retries required; crash-safety required; in-memory-only queue is NOT acceptable.
- Routing: per-repo allowlist, each repo -> exactly one channel. No fan-out, no DMs.
- Config: single YAML file loaded at startup. No hot reload, no UI.
- Secrets in .env: GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET, SLACK_BOT_TOKEN, REDIS_URL.
- Out of scope: two-way interaction, review assignment, backfill, bot commenting, config UI.
- Testing: unit tests for formatter + config loader, one integration test posting a fixture to the webhook endpoint asserting a job enqueues, plus a manual sandbox check. Retry internals lean on the queue library.

Success: a PR opened in an allowlisted repo posts a formatted summary (title, author, link, action) to the mapped channel within seconds, and a few-minute Slack outage loses no events.

Go.

assertions.text: Output proposes 2-3 distinct approaches with trade-offs
Output includes a clear recommendation with reasoning for which approach to use
A spec file is written (to references/specs/ or the designated output directory) with a descriptive name
No implementation code, project scaffolding, or package.json is created
Output includes a self-review step scanning for placeholders or contradictions
Output asks the user to review the spec before proceeding
Output offers what's-next options (implementation plan, scope another piece, etc.)
Output asks at least one clarifying question before proposing approaches
Output does not propose a full design or write a spec without first gathering requirements
Clarifying questions are presented one at a time, not as a big list
No implementation code or project scaffolding is created
